title: The Library holds what this document has, not every screenshot you ever took
goal: Open the Library in a brand new document and its Media shelf is already full of screenshots from other work, because it is showing the app wide capture folder. That is the wrong shelf: History is where everything you have ever captured lives, across every document, and the Library is meant to be what THIS document contains and can place again. Make Media show the pictures this document uses.
notes:
The bill named by the shelves prototype (http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#shelves, docs/design/modes.md section 6), settled by the user on 2026-09-15 in their own words: the split is by SCOPE, not by kind. History is the global shelf, the Library is the document own shelf.

Where it is today, verified by reading the code on 2026-09-22: Sources/Photonz/LibraryPanel.swift, header comment, Media shows the captures the app already keeps in the capture folder. That was a deliberate choice at the time so the panel was useful the first time it opened rather than four empty boxes, which is why the empty state matters here: replacing a full shelf with a blank box is a step backwards unless the blank box says what belongs there.

Not a regression and not a crash; it is the app and the settled model disagreeing about what the Library is for.
acceptance: A new empty document shows an empty Media shelf that says in plain words what will appear there, instead of captures from other documents
A picture placed in the document appears on the Media shelf, and placing it again from the shelf does not make a second copy of the file
Everything captured is still one click away in History, and nothing a person could reach before has become unreachable
A walk opens a new document, photographs the Library, places a picture, and photographs it again

log.note: Media now reads DocumentMedia (PhotonzCore, 14 tests): one tile per distinct ImageRef in the open document, newest first, canvas layer excluded so File > New opens empty. Placing reuses the ref (EditorState.placeImage), tiles drag as DocumentImageDrag (id + PNG for outside the app).
owns these walks: document-media-walk, library-walk, drop-lands-here-walk, placed-image-name-walk, shelf-scope-switch-walk

Adversarial review before building: the shelves mock says Media becomes 'the pictures this document uses' and stops there. Two things it does not answer and the app has to. (1) A blank canvas IS a picture layer, so the literal reading opens File > New on a tile of white; the shelf therefore leaves off the canvas the document is drawn on, which also makes acceptance 1 true. (2) 'The pictures this document uses' has to mean one tile per PICTURE, not per layer, or three placements of one banner are three identical tiles; the mock says exactly this two bullets earlier and it is easy to miss. Cut as decorative: nothing. Shortest version that delivers the value: the shelf, the empty line, place-again reusing the ref.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the probe: the walk caught two defects reading the code had not. Dropping a copy UNDERNEATH the Background made the Background itself a tile (the canvas rule was 'bottom layer', now 'lowest LOCKED picture') and renamed the picture's tile after the copy (the name rule was 'bottom-most', now 'the name no other name here is a numbered copy of'). Both fixed, both tested.

Left rough, not filed: the tile shows only its caption, so 'used 2 times' is readable in the tooltip and in the picked tile's section but not on the tile itself. A collage's photos are on the shelf numbered after the collage layer (Collage 1, Collage 2) and no walk drives a collage against this. Both are in the audit's rough list for the user to react to.

row-drop-slot-walk reported CRASHED once in a batch; that was my own pkill racing a probe launch while I cleaned up a duplicated walk batch, not the app. It passes on its own and passed again after. Not filed.

Media is the document's own pictures. DocumentMedia (PhotonzCore, 18 tests) decides it: one tile per picture however many layers draw it, newest first, the canvas the document is drawn on left off so File > New opens on an empty shelf that says what fills it and points at History. Placing a tile again reuses the very same picture, by double click, by Place in Picture, by a drag onto the canvas, and by a drag onto a row of the layers list (new DocumentImageDrag / DragCargo kind, PNG riding along for outside the app). Verified: Scripts/test.sh green (9152); document-media-walk (new) drives a fresh document, photographs the empty shelf, drops a picture in, places it again and proves one tile and three layers, with 6 real screen captures; library-walk, drop-lands-here-walk, placed-image-name-walk and shelf-scope-switch-walk rewritten onto the document and green, plus the drop, shelf, row-drop, paste and colour walk sets (about 45 walks). Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-23-library-media-shelf.json. Full sweep requested.
